assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling is a general method that turned aryl amine construction into a routine operation. It is visible in countless later syntheses and is used at scale in pharmaceutical process chemistry. Conceptually simple, ligand-controlled, and clearly new chemistry: the type of bond-forming method that changed how chemists everywhere build molecules.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the ligand-enabled, general catalytic amination independently and are the decisive contributors to the broad method. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor, so a two-person prize is the cleanest configuration, though the Migita/Kosugi priority question is a recognised complication.
assessment.maturity: Mature: about three decades of independent confirmation, wide industrial use and stable mechanistic understanding. Timely, arguably overdue, with the 2010 cross-coupling prize leaving this part of the field unrecognised.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views C-N coupling as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize.
Weight to give Kosugi's precursor work. I am working from memory and have not verified detailed priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened a new mode of reactivity for radical chemistry in synthesis, using mild conditions to generate open-shell intermediates and enabling reactions that were impractical before. Adoption in academic and industrial discovery chemistry is very broad and growing, and it is a real change in how bonds are made.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over many contributors. MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson published the foundational synthetic demonstrations around 2008, but Fukuzumi, Konig, Nicewicz and Melchiorre also have strong claims. A three-person prize is possible but leaves out strong contributors, and MacMillan's 2021 prize is a consideration.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature after about 15 years of use, but still evolving. Industrial impact is clear in medicinal chemistry; the field's boundaries are still moving, and recognition is timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Attribution is genuinely contested among many groups.
Whether MacMillan's recent prize weighs against him. Priority details recalled from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization, including directing-group, ligand and template control, lets chemists convert ordinary C-H bonds into C-C, C-N and C-O bonds. This has changed retrosynthetic thinking and late-stage functionalization, and uses show up in total synthesis and in industry.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand and template-enabled site selectivity), Sanford (Pd and high-valent catalysis, directed C-H) and Hartwig (borylation) contributed distinct and decisive elements. Daugulis and Smith also have strong claims, so the allocation is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Maturing. Scope and practical utility keep growing, but selectivity is still substrate-dependent and some applications are not yet routine. Slightly early compared with C-N coupling.
uncertainties: Compound discovery with several sub-strands, and attribution among the five named people is unresolved.
General practicality outside specialist labs is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that main-group combinations can activate H2 and other small molecules without a metal, which is a real conceptual novelty in bond activation. Applications in metal-free hydrogenation are real but narrower than the headline concept.
assessment.attribution: Stephan reported the first metal-free reversible H2 activation in 2006 and Erker's group contributed key early work and broadened the area, so a two-person prize is natural and clean.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed and reproduced across many labs for nearly twenty years. Practical synthetic uptake remains limited relative to transition-metal catalysis, so impact is more conceptual than methodological.
uncertainties: Breadth of synthetic use is modest.
Chemical novelty relative to earlier main-group reactivity depends on how one weighs the 2006 result.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes (NHCs and later cyclic alkyl amino carbenes) gave chemists a new ligand class and organocatalyst family. NHC ligands underpin modern olefin metathesis catalysts and cross-coupling, and the area has very broad use in synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo's 1991 isolation of a crystalline NHC is the defining event; Bertrand's earlier phosphinocarbene work and later CAAC chemistry are major. Nolan, Bode and Rovis are important for catalysis applications but later in the chain.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of confirmation and wide use. Recognition is timely or somewhat late.
uncertainties: Whether Bertrand's priority claim is as strong as Arduengo's.
Overlap with the earlier metathesis prize, since NHCs are used in Grubbs-type catalysts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation made chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins practical, extending molecule-making to polypeptides of protein size. The idea is simple and general, and uses in protein science are broad.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson introduced native chemical ligation in 1994, and Muir's expressed protein ligation extended it to semisynthesis. This is a coherent three-person configuration, with Danishefsky and others as significant but less central.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely used for decades. Timely, though some of the impact lies at the border with chemical biology.
uncertainties: Border-field question about what was new chemically versus enabling for biology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bergman's demonstration of intermolecular oxidative addition of alkane C-H bonds to iridium was a landmark of fundamental organometallic chemistry and gave the conceptual foundation for C-H functionalization. Direct synthetic application of the original system is limited.
assessment.attribution: Bergman's 1982 result is the identifiable key contribution, with Graham's contemporaneous work as a close parallel. As the candidate credits only Bergman, a single laureate is the only choice, but the parallel claim is a real issue.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and stable, with concept validated by decades of work. It is unusual to recognise this alone, as the catalytic C-H functionalization successors carry the practical impact.
uncertainties: Whether to recognise the fundamental result or the later applied methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom transfer radical polymerization gave controlled radical polymerization with predictable molecular weight and architecture using transition-metal catalysis. Its impact on polymer synthesis is large, with wide use in materials and industry.
assessment.attribution: Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto (with Kamigaito) reported the method independently in 1995, so a Matyjaszewski-Sawamoto pair, possibly with Kamigaito, is the natural configuration. Wang is a coauthor of the Matyjaszewski paper, and the RAFT and nitroxide work is competing.
assessment.maturity: Mature with extensive industrial and academic use. Timely, though the competing controlled polymerization methods complicate the prize configuration.
uncertainties: Competition with RAFT and NMP over what counts as the discovery.
Priority and authorship details recalled from memory.
